Physical AI Landscape
Research notes · 26 Sep 2026

Physical AI Landscape

About 140 companies build the robotics and physical-AI stack, in four layers.

  • Money: Figure is valued at $39B, Skild at about $14B and Physical Intelligence at $5.6B. Defense autonomy is bigger still: Anduril is reported at $61B.
  • Volume: Chinese firms shipped about 80% of the ~13,000 humanoids sold in 2025.
  • Consolidation: Amazon, Meta, Google and Mobileye bought or absorbed robot AI teams in 2024–26.
  • Data: training data is now a business of its own (Scale AI, Encord, XDOF, Midcentury).
  • Model-to-model links: no company found sells a link between two different AI models. Tensormesh shares KV caches between copies of the same model.

Every figure links to its source. Hatched bars and the weak tag mark figures from aggregator or blog reporting; check those before you rely on them. The company lists are a sample. Use the trackers at the bottom for the long tail.

Who competes with whom

Companies split by what they sell:

  • Model only: a robot brain licensed to others
  • Model + own robot: the full stack, like Figure with Helix
  • Robot, partner or undisclosed model: hardware first, using someone else's AI or not saying
  • Platform for others: models and tools that other robot makers build on

Placement follows each company's public statements. Many Chinese makers do not say which model they use.

China builds, the US funds

  • About 13,000 humanoids shipped worldwide in 2025, and Chinese firms shipped about 80% of them.
  • AgiBot led with 5,168 units, followed by Unitree and UBTech (SCMP, citing Omdia).
  • Unitree's G1 sells for about $16,000.
  • The largest valuations are American: Figure, Skild and Physical Intelligence.

Robotics venture funding reached $18.8B in 2026 so far, more than all of 2025 ($15B) and the 2021 peak ($14.1B) (Crunchbase).

Consolidation

Large companies are buying robot AI teams instead of building them.

  1. Aug 2024Amazon ← CovariantHired the founders and licensed the model (TechCrunch)
  2. Jan 2025Samsung → Rainbow RoboticsRaised its stake to 35% and became the largest shareholder (Samsung)
  3. Late 2025K-Scale Labs shuts downFailed to close its Series A and refunded preorders
  4. Jan 2026Mobileye ← Mentee RoboticsAcquisition, reported at ~$900M (PitchBook) weak
  5. Feb 2026Google ← IntrinsicMoved from Alphabet into Google to work with DeepMind (TechCrunch)
  6. May 2026Meta ← Assured Robot IntelligenceAcquisition (TechCrunch)
  7. Jul 2026Toyota Research Institute → Walden RoboticsSpin-out launched with $300M (BusinessWire)

Communication between models

Robots run a slow planning model and a fast control model. What passes between them sets three things:

  • the message size, and so whether the link can cross a network
  • how often a new message can arrive
  • whether the two models must be trained together

Prior work by field

Each piece of this problem already has prior work, usually in a field that uses a different name for it.

Robotics · hierarchical VLA Latent link from planner to controller
  • LCB, RoboDual, HiRT (2024)
  • HiRT trains the fast policy on stale latents
  • Figure Helix in production
Networking · split computing Features sent over a slow network
  • ComVLA: 16× less data, 95.4% vs 96.9% success
  • AVERY: 3 compression tiers, 94% less energy
  • Simulation only, robot to cloud
Commercial · cloud + edge Cloud planner, on-robot controller
  • Gemini Robotics: cloud model under 160 ms
  • ~250 ms end to end, 50 Hz effective (tech report)
  • What crosses the link is not published
Self-driving · collaborative perception Robots sharing compressed features
  • V2VNet (2020)
  • Where2comm (2022): over 100,000× less data
Telecom · task-oriented communication Smallest message that still works
  • Information-bottleneck approach (Shao et al.)
  • Trades bits sent against task accuracy
LLM serving · KV-cache transfer KV caches over a network
  • CacheGen compresses and streams KV caches
  • Tensormesh, $24.5M, same-model sharing
LLM multi-agent · latent communication Latent messages between models trained apart
  • C2C: 2.5× faster than text
  • LatentMAS: ~4× faster, 71–84% fewer tokens
  • Text tasks only

Closest companies

  • ZettaScale (Zenoh), Viam and Open-RMF move data between robots, fleets and the cloud.
  • Tensormesh sells KV-cache sharing between copies of one model.
  • ros-mcp-server, bb_mcp and phospho let LLM agents control robots through JSON tool calls over MCP.
  • Anduril Lattice and Shield AI Hivemind coordinate many drones inside one company's product.

Not yet checked

  • A plug-and-play adapter between two frozen robot models from different teams.
  • KV-cache transfer from planner to controller on a robot.

Assume both exist until a search in each field above says otherwise.
